name: Hospitality & Travel
tagline: Bookings, room nights, ADR, occupancy, RevPAR, cancellations and channel mix for hotels and travel businesses
description: Reservation and night-audit exports from hotel PMS and channel managers (Opera, Cloudbeds, eZee, Hotelogix, SiteMinder, STAAH), OTA extranets (Booking.com, Expedia, MakeMyTrip, Agoda, Airbnb), hotel booking-demand datasets and travel-agency booking registers.

fields.label: Booking / reservation ID
fields.description: Identifies each booking; a multi-room booking may repeat it on several rows.

fields.label: Room nights sold
fields.description: Nights × rooms per booking, or rooms sold per day in a night-audit report.

fields.label: Nightly room rate
fields.description: Price per room per night; never summed, only used to rebuild revenue.

fields.label: Rooms available
fields.description: Rooms available to sell per property per day; summed over days it gives available room nights.

subDomains.name: Reservations & bookings
subDomains.description: One row per booking with booking, check-in and check-out dates, status, channel and revenue.

subDomains.name: Daily occupancy / night audit
subDomains.description: One row per property per day with rooms available, rooms sold and room revenue.

subDomains.name: Booking demand
subDomains.description: One row per booking with a cancellation flag, lead time, nightly rate and weekend/weekday nights, as in hotel booking-demand extracts.

kpis.name: Room nights (all bookings)
kpis.definition: Room nights on every booking, before removing cancellations and no-shows.
kpis.formula: Σ nights × rooms across all bookings

variants.label: (Check-out − check-in) × rooms
variants.caveat: Nights come from the check-in and check-out dates.

variants.label: Nights (one room per booking)
variants.caveat: No rooms column, so each booking is counted as one room.

variants.label: Check-out − check-in (one room per booking)
variants.caveat: Nights come from the check-in and check-out dates, and each booking is counted as one room.

variants.label: Weekend + weekday nights
variants.caveat: Nights are weekend plus weekday nights, and each booking is counted as one room.

kpis.name: Room revenue (all bookings)
kpis.definition: Room revenue on every booking, before removing cancellations and no-shows.
kpis.formula: Σ booking revenue (or nightly rate × room nights) across all bookings

variants.label: Nightly rate × room nights
variants.caveat: No revenue column, so revenue is the nightly rate × room nights.

variants.label: Nightly rate × nights × rooms
variants.caveat: No revenue column, so revenue is the nightly rate × nights × rooms.

variants.label: Nightly rate × nights
variants.caveat: No revenue column, so revenue is the nightly rate × nights, with one room per booking.

variants.label: Nightly rate × (weekend + weekday nights)
variants.caveat: No revenue column, so revenue is the nightly rate × (weekend + weekday nights), with one room per booking.

kpis.name: Average length of stay (all bookings)
kpis.definition: Average nights per booking, before removing cancellations and no-shows.
kpis.formula: Average nights per booking

variants.label: Average (check-out − check-in)
variants.caveat: Nights come from the check-in and check-out dates.

variants.label: Average (weekend + weekday nights)
variants.caveat: Nights are weekend plus weekday nights.

kpis.name: Room revenue
kpis.definition: Room revenue from bookings that were not cancelled or no-shows.
kpis.formula: Booking revenue excluding cancelled and no-show bookings

variants.label: Excludes cancelled and no-show by status
Excludes bookings flagged cancelled
variants.caveat: Only a cancellation flag is available, so no-show bookings are still included.

variants.label: All bookings
variants.caveat: No booking status, so revenue is taken as recorded; any cancelled or no-show bookings are included.

pitfalls: Revenue lands on the date you analyse by: use the check-in or stay date for operations and the booking date for demand.

kpis.name: Occupancy
kpis.definition: Share of available room nights that were sold.
kpis.formula: Room nights sold ÷ room nights available

benchmark.note: Indicative for city hotels; resorts and seasonal markets swing much more.

pitfalls: Room nights sold and rooms available must cover the same dates and properties.

kpis.name: Average daily rate
kpis.definition: Average room revenue earned per room night sold.
kpis.formula: Room revenue ÷ room nights sold
pitfalls: ADR is revenue ÷ room nights; averaging a rate column would over-weight short stays and single-room bookings.

kpis.name: RevPAR
kpis.definition: Room revenue per available room night, combining price and occupancy.
kpis.formula: Room revenue ÷ room nights available (= ADR × occupancy)

kpis.name: Room nights sold
kpis.definition: Room nights on bookings that were not cancelled or no-shows.
kpis.formula: Σ nights × rooms, excluding cancelled and no-show bookings

variants.label: Excludes cancelled and no-show by status
Excludes bookings flagged cancelled
variants.caveat: Only a cancellation flag is available, so no-show bookings are still included.

variants.label: All bookings
variants.caveat: No booking status, so room nights are taken as recorded; any cancelled or no-show bookings are included.

kpis.name: Cancellation rate
kpis.definition: Share of bookings that were cancelled.
kpis.formula: Cancelled bookings ÷ bookings

benchmark.note: Indicative for OTA-heavy hotels; direct and non-refundable bookings cancel far less.

pitfalls: Bookings for future stays can still cancel, so recent booking months understate the final rate.

kpis.name: Bookings
kpis.definition: Number of distinct bookings made.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct booking IDs

variants.label: Row count (no booking ID)
variants.caveat: No booking ID column, so every row is counted as one booking.

kpis.name: Net bookings
kpis.definition: Bookings that were not cancelled or no-shows.
kpis.formula: Distinct bookings excluding cancelled and no-show statuses

variants.label: By cancellation flag
variants.caveat: Only a cancellation flag is available, so no-show bookings are still included.

kpis.name: No-show rate
kpis.definition: Share of bookings due to arrive whose guests never showed up.
kpis.formula: No-show bookings ÷ bookings not cancelled

kpis.name: Average length of stay
kpis.definition: Average nights per stay, on bookings that were not cancelled or no-shows.
kpis.formula: Σ nights ÷ stays (average nights per booking)

variants.label: Excludes cancelled and no-show by status
Excludes bookings flagged cancelled
variants.caveat: Only a cancellation flag is available, so no-show bookings are still included.

variants.label: All bookings
variants.caveat: No booking status, so cancelled bookings are included.

kpis.name: Average lead time
kpis.definition: Average days between booking and check-in, across all bookings.
kpis.formula: Average of (check-in date − booking date) in days

variants.label: Lead-time column
variants.caveat: Uses the lead-time column as reported.

pitfalls: Long lead times give more room to price well but usually cancel more often.

kpis.name: Direct booking share
kpis.definition: Share of bookings made through direct channels (website, phone, walk-in) rather than OTAs or agents.
kpis.formula: Direct bookings ÷ bookings
pitfalls: Check which values count as direct in Check & map › Value meanings; metasearch bookings that land on the hotel website are direct.

kpis.name: Average guest rating
kpis.definition: Average review or rating score left by guests.
kpis.formula: Average of guest rating over rated stays
pitfalls: Check the scale (out of 5 or 10) before comparing properties or benchmarks.

kpis.name: Repeat guest share
kpis.definition: Share of bookings made by guests who have stayed before.
kpis.formula: Bookings by repeat guests ÷ bookings

variants.label: Guests with 2+ bookings ÷ guests
variants.caveat: No repeat-guest flag, so this is the share of guests with two or more bookings in the file.

kpis.name: Distribution cost %
kpis.definition: OTA and agent commission as a share of room revenue.
kpis.formula: Σ commission ÷ room revenue, excluding cancelled and no-show bookings

variants.label: By cancellation flag
variants.caveat: Only a cancellation flag is available, so no-show bookings are still included.

variants.label: All bookings
variants.caveat: No booking status, so cancelled bookings are included.

kpis.name: Average booking value
kpis.definition: Room revenue per booking that was not cancelled or a no-show.
kpis.formula: Room revenue ÷ net bookings

variants.label: Room revenue ÷ bookings
variants.caveat: No status column, so the denominator includes cancelled bookings.

kpis.name: Unique guests
kpis.definition: Distinct guests who booked in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct guest IDs

charts.title: Room revenue over time
charts.reason: One revenue measure over continuous time, bucketed by check-in date so revenue sits with the stay; the soft fill shows volume without hiding the shape.

charts.title: ADR over time
charts.reason: ADR is a ratio, so it is recomputed per period (revenue ÷ room nights) and drawn as a line, never summed.

charts.title: Occupancy over time
charts.reason: Occupancy is a ratio over stay dates: recomputed per period from room nights sold and available, drawn as a line.

charts.title: RevPAR over time
charts.reason: RevPAR is a ratio, so it is recomputed per period and drawn as a line; ADR and occupancy get their own charts rather than a dual axis.

charts.title: Room revenue by channel
charts.reason: One measure across named channels: sorted horizontal bars keep OTA names readable. Top 8 plus Others.

charts.title: Room nights by room type
charts.reason: Part-to-whole across a handful of room types: a donut shows the mix at a glance.

charts.title: Bookings by status
charts.reason: A few statuses (stayed, upcoming, cancelled, no-show) as parts of all bookings: a donut shows the split.

charts.title: Cancellation rate by channel
charts.reason: A rate compared across channels: sorted bars of the recomputed rate, with channels under 30 bookings hidden as too small.

charts.title: Cancellation rate by lead time
charts.reason: Do early bookings cancel more? The recomputed cancellation rate per lead-time band, in band order.

charts.title: How far ahead guests book
charts.reason: The spread of booking lead times: a histogram of bookings per lead-time band shows the booking window.

charts.title: Room nights by arrival weekday
charts.reason: Seven ordered weekdays and one measure: columns show the business-versus-leisure arrival rhythm.

charts.title: ADR vs occupancy by hotel
charts.reason: Two measures per hotel: a scatter shows which properties trade rate for occupancy, without a misleading dual axis.

pitfalls: ADR, occupancy and RevPAR are ratios of totals: recompute them from room nights and revenue for every period and group, never average daily or per-booking rates.
Cancelled and no-show bookings must be excluded from room nights and revenue, or ADR and occupancy are overstated.
Occupancy and RevPAR need rooms available for the same dates and properties as the room nights sold.
A stay is counted on its check-in date; long stays that cross a month end are not split across months.
Future stays can still cancel or change, so the latest booking months understate cancellations and overstate revenue on the books.
